about: Negative controls for the witness branch. Expected values are what each implementation DID on 2026-10-12, not what it should do: a row labelled requirement whose verify_py value contradicts its spec note is a pinned known divergence, so the runner stays green until someone changes behaviour on purpose and updates this file in the same commit.

strict_about: Added 2026-10-16 after Aura c109326 (#8890): the pinned columns record what each implementation DID, so a green default run documents a divergence rather than surfacing it. `strict` records what the spec REQUIRES, on requirement rows (MUST or SHOULD) and on proposed-requirement rows (PROPOSED). `python3 controls/negative-controls.py --strict` judges every implementation that ran against `strict` instead of the pin and exits 1 if any MUST or SHOULD row fails; `--strict --proposed` also fails on PROPOSED rows. Choice rows have no strict value. Matcher keys: verdict (must equal), not_verdict (must differ), exit (must equal), exit_not (must differ).
